report: Constructed a differential reproducer to test the missing `mstateen0[62]` (ENVCFG) gating on S-mode `senvcfg` accesses. The tests configure PMP, set `menvcfg.CBZE`, drop to S-mode, and perform a `csrr` from `0x10A` (`senvcfg`). In the positive control (`control.S`), M-mode enables `mstateen0[62]=1`, allowing S-mode access. In the test (`test.S`), M-mode clears `mstateen0[62]=0`. According to the RISC-V State Enable (Smstateen) extension, S-mode attempts to access `senvcfg` while `mstateen0[62]==0` must raise an Illegal Instruction exception (mcause=2). Spike properly raises this exception, which is caught and mapped to a PASS (`tohost=1`) by the trap handler. Wally incorrectly permits the access without trapping, resulting in test fallthrough and a FAIL (`tohost=3`).
evidence: RTL lacks an M-mode State Enable check during Privilege Mode < M accesses to the `senvcfg` CSR (0x10A), allowing unauthorized environments to improperly read/write configurations. The provided assembly successfully catches the failure by observing the absence of expected trap routing to `mtvec`.
